remove: The coloured glass-and-garnish glyphs on every serve line. They are a second, skeuomorphic illustration grammar next to the linear contour/hilera system, and they push each serve line 18 px off the column's left edge.
top_problem: The furrow-grid thesis promises a strict survey ruling, but the front is built on content-driven unequal columns (271.5/235.6/211.6 px), plus a separate 4-up zero-proof grid and a third grid on the back (49/350/555). Items that share a hilera do not share a serve-line baseline. So the literal 'every drink planted in its row' is not literal, and the boldest missing idea is one modular field grid that the contours visibly resolve into, used on both pages.
fixes: Put the front on one modular grid of three equal columns (about 239 px pitch from 49.33 to 767.98), set zero proof on the same three columns or a 6-unit subdivision of them, and put the back's beer/cans/wine columns on the same x values.
Lock each hilera's serve line (garnish · glass) to a shared baseline per row, set by the deepest item in that row, so row-mates end together on the furrow and do not float 16 px apart.
Remove the glass glyphs, or hang them in the ring gutter, so the serve line starts at the column's left edge of 49.33/320.84/556.41 px and not 18 px in.

Fix the ingredient runts ('soda', 'lime', 'fresh lime', 'mineral water', 'pineapple') by rebalancing the line breaks or using a no-break between the final two ingredients, and make the section head clearly larger than the 16 px names (at least 22-24 px, or a distinct cut) so the header level reads as its own level.

On the back, widen the class column or abbreviate 'mezcal espadín joven' to clear NOM by at least one em, and snap the SIDRA and ESPUMOSOS subheads onto the same row grid as the draft column (they sit 2 px off).

top_problem: The field thesis is strong and the back-page oak-age chart is ownable, but the typography does not carry it. 'Cantina' is a default Newsreader regular sitting on a rule and does nothing with rows or furrows. Section heads are barely larger than the bold item names, so hierarchy is flat. The level-2 heads use 5-word tracked caps that break the proposal's own avoid-list. Five of twelve cocktails end their ingredient line on a one-word widow. The mixed price format (11.50 among integers) caps criterion 3. Boldest missing idea: make the wordmark itself the planted row. Set 'Cantina' on the furrow with its letterforms or baseline taken from the hilera, so the type becomes the field and not a caption under it.
remove: The art-legend swatches and north arrow on the front ('Contour strips · Iowa', 'Agave hileras · Jalisco'). Explaining the illustration with a map key is a conceit that competes with the proposal-ring key, which does real work. Also drop the redundant 'class' column on the spirits table, since the subhead already says blanco, reposado or añejo.
fixes: Set every price in one format: either print 11.50 as '11½' or give all prices two decimals, with tabular lining figures in both inline and table prices.

Rebuild the section-head level to at least 1.6x the item-name size (about 26-28 px) or a clearly different weight and colour, and shorten the tracked-caps subheads to 3 words or fewer (e.g. 'POR COPA', 'DE BARRIL', 'CASA'), putting the English in the italic.

Set ingredient lines to break without one-word widows: rebalance the 3-col measure, tighten the tracking of the condensed sans slightly, or allow manual breaks at the '·' separators so no line ends on 'soda', 'lime' or 'pineapple'.

Put both pages on one column grid: move back col 2 from x 350.1 to 320.8, snap wine to 556.4, give the zero-proof row the 3-col grid (or a declared 4-col subgrid that shares the 49.3 and 556.4 edges), and unify table and list item names at one size.

Redraw the wordmark as part of the field: 'Cantina' in a heavier or custom-cut display that sits on and interrupts the first furrow with purpose, with '& Cocktail Bar · Iowa City' locked to its baseline as a set lockup, not a floating condensed caption with rule stubs on both sides.

The oak scale bar is in survey red, but the oak data bars are brown, which breaks the promise that red means price. fixes: Make the colour mapping hold: keep survey red for prices only, and draw the oak scale-bar key in the same #7A3F27 brown as the oak bars. Or drop red from prices, set them in ink Plex 500 tabular, and keep red for a single accent, so the prices stand out through figure style rather than colour repetition.

Separate the two reds. Push red earth toward a browner, darker ochre-rust (about #7E4A33 at lower chroma), or shift survey red cooler (about #A4161A), so prices and the earth bands stop reading as two near-miss tones of one colour.
Fix price format consistency: Ranch Water 11.50 is the only decimal. Either ask Rob to confirm a whole-dollar price or set every price to one format. Do not change the value without approval.

Put Zero Proof on the 3-column grid used above, or make the 4-column pitch share the same column origins, and match back Cans x (350.1) to the front column 2 origin (320.8), so one grid runs across both pages.

Reduce the two front hileras divider bands to hairline furrow rules or a single-row rosette line at half height, so the section heads (13 pt) out-rank the dividers. Redraw the agave rosettes as true plan-view rosettes of varied size rather than a tiled blue-green asterisk, so the field no longer reads as a woven blanket border.

remove: The two agave-star section-divider bands on the front. They repeat the hero as bunting and break the 'one gesture' rule in the thesis. Separate the sections with spacing or a single furrow hairline.
top_problem: The thesis is ownable and clever: Iowa contour strips lock into Jalisco agave hileras, set out as a survey plate. The execution does not deliver it. Across the room the hero reads as a striped serape or blanket border with asterisk stitching, which is the costume the avoid-list bans. It needs a legend to explain itself, and below it is a conventional 3-column list with rules. The boldest missing idea is to let the field become the page. The drinks should be planted along the contour strips themselves, so the reading rows bend with the land at the top and straighten into hileras as the eye goes down. The concept would then govern the geometry and reading path, instead of decorating a header. Against Solstice, Glass Garden and ref-01, it lacks scale contrast, depth and material richness: flat vector bands against layered, crafted art.
fixes: Redraw the field so it reads as aerial terrain, not a serape. Make the relief dominant and asymmetric: fewer, wider strips, varied strip widths, and rosettes drawn in plan view at varied scale and spacing that shrink with distance. Drop the uniform teal asterisks, which read as blanket stitching.

Make the concept govern the structure. Carry at least one contour line from the hero into the menu, so the first section's row rules visibly inherit its curve and relax to straight. As it stands, the hero and the list are two unrelated systems.

Remove the front star-band dividers. Give the back a real field moment instead of the thin striped head band. For example, the spirits table could sit on the straight hileras at a larger scale, so the page has one focal image and quiet zones.
Put Sin alcohol on the 3-column grid, align the back's Cans column with the front column-2 edge, and stop the furrow rules at the text margin instead of bleeding them off the trim edge.

Detach the proposal rings from the previous item's rule by ending each rule a gutter short of the ring. Replace the coloured glass-icon family with glyphs in the contour hairline grammar, or cut them. They are a second illustration style.

remove: The north arrows and the 'Contour strips · Iowa / Agave hileras · Jalisco' legend swatches, above all the copy dropped mid-scroll on the phone.
top_problem: The phone is the print layout poured into one column: the oak-age axis loses its scale, the print legend lands mid-scroll, and beer and wine sit under 25 spirit rows with no section navigation.
fixes: Phone oak marks: print a 0-12-24-36 tick strip under each spirits sub-head, draw every mark on one fixed-width track, enlarge the unaged dot and 'age not stated' dash, and move the House Blanco dot off its sensory line.
Phone reading path: add a sticky or top section index styled as furrow labels, and move Cerveza/Vino ahead of the spirits table or collapse spirits by class.
Remove the mid-scroll front legend and the north arrows on phone; keep only the proposal-ring key, once, under the wordmark.
Put Sin alcohol back on the 3-column grid, snap the back's beer and wine columns to the front's x positions, and end Draft, Cans/Cider and Wine on the same furrow.
Settle the level-2 head rule so every tracked-caps sub-head either carries its inline italic class line or none does, and render 'Destilados · Spirits' as a level-1 head on phone.

lens: every item and price against expanded-v1/manifest.json
top_problem: All 50 items and prices on the letter pages match the manifest. The 12 cocktails, 25 spirits, 4 draft beers, 1 can, 1 cider, 3 wines and 4 zero-proof drinks are all there. Every PROPOSED and rob_reference_image row has a ring, and no approved_db row has one. But the non-cocktail categories are thin and unflagged. The beers have no ABV. Malbec and Pinot Grigio say 'Dry red wine' and 'Dry white wine', which are category labels with no grape region or producer. Brut Rosé does not say glass or bottle (manifest needs_input 5). Agua de Jamaica, Horchata, Nojito and Jarritos have a sensory line only, with no ingredient line. None of these gaps is flagged as missing_ingredients. The four mezcal prices are placeholders in the manifest, yet they print as firm prices with only the generic 'proposed' ring. Beer and wine are also squeezed into the bottom third of the back under a 25-row spirits table, so the categories are not treated equally.
problems: Criterion 8: none of the 4 draft beers or the Tecate can shows an ABV, and the menu does not flag it as missing. The descriptions are style only ('Crisp pale lager', 'Hop-forward draft IPA').

Criterion 8: Malbec 'Dry red wine', Pinot Grigio 'Dry white wine' and Brut Rosé 'Dry sparkling rosé' read like database categories. They give no region or producer and no flag. A guest cannot choose from them.
Brut Rosé 13 prints as a plain price. The manifest says glass or bottle is unknown (needs_input 5), and the menu gives no pour label and no flag.

Mezcal prices for Montelobos (12), Ilegal Joven (13) and 400 Conejos (10) are marked 'PRICE PLACEHOLDER' in the manifest. They print with the same ring as a sourced proposal, so a placeholder price cannot be told apart from a researched one.

Zero proof: Nojito, Agua de Jamaica, Horchata and Jarritos have only the italic sensory line. Rob's binding stack is name/price, then sensory, then ingredients, then garnish · glass; these four stop after the sensory line, with no ingredient line and no flag. Jarritos says 'ask for flavors', which is service copy, not a description.
Criterion 3: 'Ranch Water 11.50' is the only price with decimals. All other prices are whole numbers, so the format is mixed.

Criterion 3: on the back table, price sits at the far right, about 1350 px from the name at 300 dpi. The furrow row rules and tabular figures keep each price tied to its row, so association passes. Eye travel is still the longest on the menu.

Criterion 5: the reading order is cocktails, zero proof (front), then spirits, beer and wine (back). Zero proof comes before every other alcohol category, and wine ends in the bottom-right corner with three items. The spirits table takes about 65% of the back, and beer and wine read as leftovers.

Legend label 'months in oak (NOM class)' also covers the Cognac VSOP arrow. VSOP is not a NOM-006 class, so the legend misstates the source of that one mark. It traces to the manifest's own sensory line, so this is not a gate failure.

Casa house pours ('Blanco Tequila', 'Añejo Tequila') print with '—' for NOM and region and no brand, which reads as a hole in the data table. Per the manifest this is correct, but the menu does not flag it.
fixes: Put 'ABV — pending' (or the real ABV once supplied) on every beer, and grape · region (or 'region — pending') on each wine, so the missing facts are flagged, not hidden behind category labels.
Label Brut Rosé 'glass' or 'bottle' once Rob answers needs_input 5, and flag it as pending in this proof until then.
Mark the three placeholder mezcal prices with a separate key, such as a hollow price or '$ tbc', so they are not shown as firm prices.
Add an ingredient line to Agua de Jamaica, Horchata and Nojito from known facts or flag it pending, and replace 'ask for flavors' with the actual Jarritos flavour list or a flagged gap.

Print Ranch Water as 11.5 or round it with Rob's approval so every price uses one format, and give beer and wine a band the same weight as the others, or move zero proof after wine, so the categories get equal treatment.

lens: ingredient names, sensory lines, description completeness
top_problem: The cocktail stack is well done, but every other category is thin, and the gaps are not flagged. Wine has no region or producer: Malbec is described only as 'Dry red wine', Pinot Grigio as 'Dry white wine', and Brut Rosé has no grape and no glass-or-bottle label, even though the manifest marks that as needs_input. Beer lists no ABV, and three beer lines just repeat the item name ('Hop-forward draft IPA', 'Toasty amber lager', 'Dry sparkling cider'). Zero-proof drinks have no ingredient or serve line. Several cocktail specs are incomplete as printed: a 'Spicy Pineapple Margarita' with no lime, sweetener or orange liqueur; a Manhattan with no bitters; 'ginger' in Loess without saying what form. The manifest matches exactly (50 of 50 items and prices, and the ring key is on every PROPOSED or rob_reference_image row), so the content is accurate. It is not complete, and nothing flags missing_ingredients.
problems: Wine (Malbec, Pinot Grigio, Brut Rosé) has no region, producer or vintage. Brut Rosé sits under 'Espumosos · Sparkling' at 13 with no pour label, although the manifest note says glass or bottle is unknown (needs_input 5). Nothing on the page flags this.

Beer and cider list no ABV anywhere and no brewery. 'Hop-forward draft IPA', 'Toasty amber lager' and 'Dry sparkling cider' mostly repeat the item name. An Iowa City cantina with unnamed draft beers reads like a generic menu.

Zero proof (Nojito, Agua de Jamaica, Horchata, Jarritos) has only a sensory line. There is no ingredient line and no serve line, so this category is treated worse than cocktails and breaks Rob's item stack.

The Spicy Pineapple Margarita prints only 'jalapeño-infused tequila blanco · fresh pineapple' and a bare 'rocks'. A margarita with no citrus, sweetener or modifier reads as an incomplete spec, not a recipe. The Manhattan has no bitters. Loess lists 'ginger' without saying whether it is fresh, syrup or beer. The design copies the manifest faithfully but none of these rows is flagged missing_ingredients.
Carajillo and the Spicy Pineapple Margarita show only a glass on the serve line, with no garnish and no 'no garnish' intent. Next to fully specified neighbours they look unfinished.

Every sensory line is marked draft_not_tasted in the manifest, including those on approved_db items (Manhattan, Brown Butter Old Fashioned, House Daiquiri). They print as settled tasting notes with no ring, so the proposal key under-reports what still needs sign-off.

Montelobos, Ilegal Joven and 400 Conejos carry PRICE PLACEHOLDER notes in the manifest but print as firm prices (12, 13, 10). The only mark is the same ring used for any proposed item, so a guest or Rob cannot tell a placeholder price from a proposed item.
Mixed price format: Ranch Water prints '11.50' and every other price is a whole number.
The back legend reads 'months in oak (NOM class)', but Cognac VSOP is plotted on the same axis with an off-scale arrow. NOM-006 does not govern cognac, so the legend mislabels one row.

The house pours (Blanco Tequila, Añejo Tequila) name no brand, and 'Blanco Tequila' repeats its class column word for word. The seven blanco brands share one class-level tasting line, which is honest, but it means brand choice rests on price alone.

Category balance and order: cocktails and zero proof fill the front, spirits take about 70% of the back, and beer and wine are squeezed into the bottom quarter. Wine gets 3 items with one-word descriptions. The reading path works, but the categories are not treated equally.
fixes: Add wine region and producer for Malbec and Pinot Grigio, and the grape and region for Brut Rosé, plus a 'copa' or 'botella' label on Brut Rosé. Where the data does not exist, print a visible missing_ingredients or needs_input flag in the proposal key rather than 'Dry red wine'.
Add ABV and brewery to every beer and cider, and replace sensory lines that repeat the name with real style notes. If ABV is unknown, flag it in the key.

Give zero-proof drinks the same item stack as cocktails, with an ingredient line and a garnish · glass line (for example, Nojito: mint, fresh lime, simple syrup, soda; mint sprig · highball), taken from verified recipes or flagged.

Add a second key mark (for example, a filled or half ring) for placeholder prices and for untasted draft sensory lines, so the three mezcal placeholders and every draft_not_tasted line are visibly pending and not presented as settled.

Send the Spicy Pineapple Margarita (no citrus, sweetener or modifier), the Manhattan (no bitters), the ingredient 'ginger' in Loess and the missing garnishes on Carajillo and the Spicy Pineapple Margarita back to Rob as missing_ingredients. Also relabel the oak legend so Cognac VSOP is not described as a NOM class.

lens: Flow and reading path for a Mexican restaurant and cocktail bar in Iowa City, across front and back
top_problem: The flow is sound on the front and then falls apart on the back. The front reads well: field, then wordmark, then Clásicos, then De la Casa, then Sin alcohol. On the back, the 25-row spirits table takes about 70% of the page. Beer, cider and wine, which are the volume categories for a Mexican restaurant in a college town (Modelo, Tecate), are pushed into a cramped strip at the bottom. There the columns end at different heights and the lines are taxonomy filler ('Dry red wine', 'Crisp pale lager'): no ABV, no wine region, and no missing_ingredients flag. So the drinks categories are not treated equally, and the reader's path ends in a table and a legend instead of a finish. The item content itself is clean. All 50 items and prices match expanded-v1/manifest.json, and every PROPOSED and rob_reference_image row carries the ring key.
problems: Criterion 3: the price format is mixed. 'Ranch Water 11.50' is the only price with decimals among whole-dollar prices. It matches the manifest's 11.5, but the format is not consistent.

Criterion 3: on the back, prices sit at the far right of the table. Eye travel from name to price is about 75% of the measure. Each row has its furrow rule, so it passes, but it is long travel for a guest who just wants a price.

Criterion 5: on the front, the furrow rule after each price runs straight into the next column's proposal ring and name ('Margarita 15 ____ o Paloma 12'). That pulls the eye sideways across the three columns instead of down each item stack, and makes the ring look like a leader target.
Criterion 5: Sin alcohol switches from the 3-column grid to 4 columns and drops the ingredient line. It reads like a footnote, not a section equal to the others.

Criterion 5: in the back table, 'Casa · House pours' comes before the tequila classes and puts Cognac VSOP (off-scale arrow, NOM and region dashes) inside a tequila survey. That breaks the blanco, reposado, añejo, mezcal progression the oak axis sets up.

Criterion 5: the back columns are unbalanced. Draft runs 4 deep, while Cans/Cider and Wine end high, leaving a dead field above the legend. There is also about 5% dead paper under the legend on both pages.

Criterion 8: beer lists style but no ABV. Wine lists grape but no region (Malbec, Pinot Grigio), and Brut Rosé has neither grape nor region. None of these gaps is flagged as missing_ingredients on the menu or in the proposal's open questions.
Criterion 8: zero-proof items have a sensory line but no ingredient line (Nojito, Agua de Jamaica, Horchata), which breaks Rob's item stack. Jarritos has 'ask for flavors' with no flavor list.
Criterion 8: the manifest labels the four mezcal prices as placeholders, but on the menu they look the same as confirmed prices. The ring only says 'proposed', not 'price placeholder'.

Criterion 10: the back page is two design languages. A Tufte data table sits on top of the front's card-stack style for beer and wine, and the beer/wine block feels bolted on rather than surveyed like the rest.
fixes: Rebalance the back: shorten the spirits table's row height, or move the House pours strip to a narrow side band, and give Beer & cider and Wine equal full-width bands with balanced column heights that end on a common baseline.

Add ABV to every beer and region to every wine (grape and region for Brut Rosé). Where the manifest has no data, print or log a visible missing_ingredients flag and ask Rob. Do not ship the taxonomy lines 'Dry red wine' or 'Crisp pale lager' as descriptions.
End each front furrow rule at the price, or stop it short of the next column's gutter ring, so the reading path runs down each item stack and not across into the neighbouring drink.

Put Sin alcohol on the same 3-column grid with a full item stack (ingredient line from the manifest, or a flagged gap), and make the price format consistent across the menu (for example, print 11.50 as the only non-integer on purpose, or ask Rob to set a whole-dollar price).
Move Cognac VSOP out of the tequila survey into its own 'Otros' row after mezcal, and mark the four mezcal prices as placeholders separately from the 'proposed' ring.
not_reviewed: The phone render (preview-phone.png) was not opened; the phone content check relies on gates.json (50/50 items on phone).

lens: voice and consistency of descriptions, bilingual headings and venue copy, venue-type fit
top_problem: The description system falls apart below the cocktails. The 12 cocktails get the full binding stack: sensory line, role-ordered ingredients, garnish and glass. Zero-proof gets one italic line with no ingredients or glass. Beer and cider get taxonomy lines with no ABV. Wine gets 'Dry red wine' and 'Dry white wine' with no region. None of these gaps is flagged. The categories are not treated equally, and the voice changes from sensory three-beats to database classes.
problems: Criterion 8: Nojito, Agua de Jamaica, Horchata and Jarritos show only a sensory line. There is no ingredient line and no garnish · glass line, so the binding item stack is broken for a whole section. 'Mint, lime, soda' is doing the job of both the sensory line and the ingredients.

Criterion 8: none of the 6 beer and cider rows shows an ABV, and Malbec, Pinot Grigio and Brut Rosé show no region. No missing_ingredients / needs-input marker is printed. The only mark is the proposal ring, which covers status, not missing facts.

Voice: the beer and wine lines read as taxonomy and repeat the item name: 'Hop-forward draft IPA', 'Crisp pale lager', 'Dry red wine', 'Dry white wine', 'Dry sparkling cider', 'Dry sparkling rosé'. Modelo's line is twice as long as its neighbours. Jarritos uses a semicolon and a service instruction ('ask for flavors'). The Margarita is the only cocktail not written as a three-beat line ('Bright and citrus-forward'). This is at least three voices on one sheet.

Every cocktail sensory line is manifest sensory_status draft_not_tasted, and some go past the ingredient list: Loess 'ginger snap', Milpa 'cacao, oak', Mezcal Negroni 'velvet'. They come from the manifest, so this is not a gate fail, but they print as authoritative tasting notes with no draft marker.

Bilingual headings are inconsistent in case and length: 'De la Casa' uses title case but 'Sin alcohol' and 'Cerveza y sidra' use sentence case (Spanish would be 'De la casa'). The Tequila · Blanco/Reposado/Añejo subheads are not bilingual pairs but Casa · House pours is. 'MEZCAL' stands alone. 'POR COPA · BY THE GLASS' is 5 tracked-caps words, which breaks the proposal's own avoid-list rule of no tracked caps longer than 3 words.

Spirits table: the legend says 'months in oak (NOM class)', but Cognac VSOP is not a NOM class and is plotted on the same axis with an off-scale arrow. The NOM column is all em-dashes for the four mezcals, and the region column is about half dashes. At arm's length this reads as unfinished data, not a deliberate unknown. Region granularity is mixed: 'Los Altos' and 'Tequila Valley' sit beside the state 'Guanajuato'.

Order: the mezcal group runs 11, 12, 13, then 10 (400 Conejos is after Ilegal Joven), while every tequila group ascends by price. Ilegal's own sensory line splits the group, so 400 Conejos reads as an afterthought.
Criterion 3: Ranch Water is the only decimal price ('11.50'); every other price is a whole number. The '$' column head appears only on the back table, so the price format differs between pages.

Criterion 5 / category equality: 25 spirit rows fill about 60% of the back. Beer, cider and wine are packed into the bottom band, and wine has only 3 rows in the right third with dead space under it. The front also ends with an empty band under the legend. The order (cocktails, zero-proof, spirits, beer, wine) fits a cantina, but zero-proof sitting mid-sequence on the front, with half the item stack, reads like a footnote.
Taglines and captions: the legend captions 'Contour strips · Iowa' and 'Agave hileras · Jalisco' describe the art, not items. The venue line matches the brief. There are no slogans, so this passes.
fixes: Give zero-proof the full binding stack: add ingredient lines and garnish · glass lines from the manifest, and print a quiet 'recipe pending' flag wherever a field is null, instead of dropping the line.

Add ABV to every beer and cider row and a region to every wine row. Where the manifest has no value, print a visible needs-input mark (for example 'ABV —' with a key entry) rather than leaving the fact out silently.

Rewrite the beer, cider and wine sensory lines in the same three-beat sensory voice as the cocktails, without repeating the style name, and cut Modelo's line and Jarritos' 'ask for flavors' to fit that voice. Rewrite them only from sourced facts or flag them.

Standardise the bilingual headings: use Spanish sentence case throughout ('De la casa'), make every subhead a Spanish · English pair or make none of them pairs, and shorten 'POR COPA · BY THE GLASS' to 3 tracked-caps words or fewer (for example 'COPA · GLASS').

Sort the mezcal group by price like the tequila groups, move Cognac VSOP out of the NOM oak axis or relabel the legend 'months in oak', and show Ranch Water as 11.5 or in a price format that matches the other prices.

lens: missing data: proposed rows, placeholders, unknown regions, Brut Rosé glass/bottle gap, invention
top_problem: K1 has one flag, the ring, and uses it for every kind of missing data. The ring means 'row pending approval', but on the print menu it also has to cover prices with no evidence, regions nobody has verified, an unknown serve size, missing ABVs and incomplete recipes. Montelobos 12, Ilegal Joven 13 and 400 Conejos 10 have price_evidence null and are marked 'PRICE PLACEHOLDER' in the manifest, yet they print in the same red tabular figures as the corpus-median tequila prices. The Brut Rosé 13 (needs_input 5: glass or bottle unknown) prints with no serve label and no flag. The designer says in proposal.md line 110 that 'the manifest's note fields are not printed'. So the known gaps are printed as facts, and that fails content_integrity.
problems: Mezcal placeholder prices (Montelobos Espadín 12, Ilegal Joven 13, 400 Conejos Espadín 10) print with the same weight as evidenced prices. The only mark is the generic proposal ring, and nothing tells a guest or Rob that these numbers have no source. proposal.md line 110 also says 'four mezcal prices are placeholders', but Del Maguey Vida 11 has evidence (Rob's six-panel ref $11), so only three are placeholders. The designer's own gap report is inaccurate.

Brut Rosé 13 sits under 'ESPUMOSOS · SPARKLING' with no glass/bottle/pour label and no flag. The manifest marks it 'glass or bottle unknown (needs_input 5)'. Nearby it is Malbec and Pinot Grigio under 'POR COPA · BY THE GLASS', so a reader will assume $13 is a glass. That is an unflagged guess about the serve.

Unknown regions and NOMs print as a bare em dash (Espolòn, Milagro, Casamigos, Hornitos, Teremana, Clase Azul region; Casa Noble NOM and region). The legend defines '–' only as 'age not stated' in the oak column. In the table columns a dash reads as 'not applicable' or 'none', not as 'unknown, to be verified'. The manifest's region_note says regions must be 'verified before print', and nothing on the page says the printed regions are unverified.

The data contradicts itself and nothing flags it. Hornitos Reposado (NOM 1102) shows region '—', while Tres Generaciones Añejo, also NOM 1102, shows 'Tequila Valley'. One distillery appears with two region states, so the region column is visibly unreliable.

Cocktails with incomplete recipes print as if they were complete. Spicy Pineapple Margarita shows only 'jalapeño-infused tequila blanco · fresh pineapple', a margarita with no citrus or modifier, although the manifest says 'confirm liqueur/citrus'. It and Carajillo also have no garnish (garnish null) and show only 'rocks', with no flag. Milpa Old Fashioned and Loess say 'recipe to be written and costed' but carry only the same ring as a fully specified Paloma.

Beer has no ABV anywhere (Czech Pilsner, Dry-Hopped IPA, Amber Lager, Modelo, Tecate, Dry Cider). Wine has no region (Malbec, Pinot Grigio, Brut Rosé), and its descriptions are taxonomy ('Dry red wine', 'Dry white wine'). Criterion 8 requires style + ABV and grape + region; the data is missing and there is no missing_ingredients flag on the page.
Brown Butter Old Fashioned has an unconfirmed dairy allergen (needs_input 1) and no marker. This is a guest-safety gap.

Every sensory line in the manifest is draft_not_tasted, and every spirit sensory line is a class-level template (all seven blancos share 'Unaged · peppery, bright cooked agave'). They print as tasting notes. The class-level line appears once per section head, which is honest, but the house-pour rows repeat it as if it were an item note.

The ring does not distinguish rob_reference_image (Rob's own board: Paloma, Ranch Water, Mezcal Negroni, Modelo, Tecate, Nojito, Jarritos, Del Maguey Vida) from PROPOSED_needs_rob_approval (designer inventions such as Batanga, Carajillo, Milpa, Loess, all 22 other spirits). Rob cannot see at a glance which rows he supplied and which are new asks.

Ring placement is ambiguous in the cocktail grid. The rings for Paloma, Ranch Water, Batanga, Carajillo and the others sit at the end of the previous column's leader rule, so the Paloma ring looks like the end of Margarita's rule. The association is weak, though not wrong enough to fail the gate.
Price format is mixed. Ranch Water prints 11.50; every other price is a whole number.

Nothing was invented beyond the manifest. All 50 items, prices, ingredients, garnish, glass, class, NOM and region match (gates.json content 50/50), and the legend captions ('Contour strips · Iowa', 'Agave hileras · Jalisco') describe the devices, not items. The failure is presenting known gaps as facts, not making things up.
fixes: Give placeholder prices their own mark: print Montelobos, Ilegal Joven and 400 Conejos prices in a hollow or muted style with a '†' keyed to 'price placeholder — set before print' (or print 'TBD' instead of a number), and correct proposal.md to say three placeholders, not four.
Give Brut Rosé an explicit serve slot, for example 'Brut Rosé · glass/bottle ? 13' with a needs-input mark keyed in the legend, or move it into a 'serve TBC' state until needs_input 5 is answered.

Separate 'unknown' from 'not applicable' in the spirits table: use '?' or a hairline open square for unverified region/NOM, add 'region not verified' to the legend, and resolve or flag the Hornitos/Tres Generaciones NOM 1102 region contradiction.

Add a second key mark alongside the ring: one glyph for Rob-reference rows and another for designer-proposed rows. Add a 'recipe incomplete' mark on Spicy Pineapple Margarita, Milpa Old Fashioned and Loess, a 'garnish TBC' mark on Carajillo and Spicy Pineapple, and a dairy allergen mark on Brown Butter Old Fashioned.

Add missing_ingredients flags where beer ABV and wine grape and region are unknown (for example 'ABV —?' and 'region —?'), replace 'Dry red wine' and 'Dry white wine' with the grape name plus a flagged region slot, and standardise Ranch Water to one price format with a note to Rob.

lens: ingredient, garnish, glass, NOM and region traceability; description quality; venue fit; description-price layout
top_problem: All 50 items trace to the manifest, and all 18 printed NOMs match public.brands.primary_nom. The menu still falls short in three ways. (1) It leaves out or blanks facts that the database has. (2) The beer, wine and spirit lines are taxonomy labels, not guest copy. (3) The front-page ingredient lines break inside ingredient names ('grapefruit / soda', 'fresh / lime', 'fresh / pineapple', 'sparkling / mineral water', 'house / demerara syrup', 'honey / syrup', 'roasted-corn / syrup'). That third problem breaks Rob's ingredient-stack rule on nearly half the cocktails.
problems: VERIFIED: 4 approved cocktails against phg.recipe_versions via menu_items.current_recipe_version_id. Margarita rv f06abb74: Rocks, Lime wheel. Manhattan rv 9fb77eaa: Coupe, Cocktail cherry. House Daiquiri rv 14d45e57: Coupe, Lime coin. Brown Butter Old Fashioned rv 7095fd3d: Rocks, Orange peel. The printed garnish and glass match on all four. The Margarita sensory line 'Bright and citrus-forward' matches phg.menu_items.menu_description.

VERIFIED NOMs, public.brands.primary_nom: Espolon 1440, Olmeca Altos 1111, Milagro 1559, Patron 1492, Siete Leguas 1120, Casamigos 1609, Don Julio 1449 (Blanco and 1942), Hornitos 1102, Cazadores 1487, Teremana 1613, Corralejo 1368, Herradura 1119, Fortaleza 1493, Clase Azul 1595, Tres Generaciones 1102, El Tesoro 1139. All match the printed values.
OMITTED FACT: Casa Noble Reposado prints NOM '—'. brands 'Casa Noble' is null, but 'Cn Casa Noble' and 'Marques de Casa Noble' both carry primary_nom 1137. A sourced NOM is being printed as unknown.

OMITTED FACT: Manhattan prints 'rye whiskey · sweet vermouth'. The approved guest copy in phg.menu_items (rv 9fb77eaa) reads 'Rye, sweet vermouth, aromatic bitters.' The manifest hides the bitters as 'public_components'. The printed build is therefore incomplete against the venue's own approved description, and it breaks the role order (bitters is a role). The Brown Butter Old Fashioned prints its bitters, so the two cocktails are handled inconsistently.

REGION INCONSISTENCY: Hornitos Reposado prints region '—' while Tres Generaciones Añejo, on the same NOM 1102 (Casa Sauza), prints 'Tequila Valley'. Same distillery, two different region states. Region has no DB column; it is a design-lead claim marked 'verify before print' in the manifest. The regions printed are correct as far as I can tell (Los Altos for 1111/1120/1139/1449/1487/1492, Tequila Valley for 1119/1493, Guanajuato for 1368, Oaxaca for all four mezcals), but they are not verified in the database.

AGE MARK INCONSISTENCY: Ilegal Joven gets the 'unaged' dot, while Del Maguey Vida, Montelobos Espadín and 400 Conejos Espadín get the 'age not stated' dash. All four are unaged espadín jóvenes. The manifest cls lacks 'joven' on three of them, so this is sourced but misleading.

CLASS OVERREACH: the oak scale bar is captioned 'months in oak (NOM class)', but Cognac VSOP sits on the same axis with an arrow. VSOP age comes from the cognac appellation rules, not NOM-006, and the manifest's sensory_status wrongly attributes it to NOM-006. Also, blanco is printed as 'Unaged', but NOM-006 allows blanco to rest up to 2 months. 'Unaged' is the common guest shorthand but not strictly the class definition.

DESCRIPTION QUALITY (12): the cocktail sensory lines are strong and in one voice ('Cola-dark, salty, sharp lime', 'Toasted corn, cacao, oak'). But 'Dry red wine', 'Dry white wine', 'Crisp pale lager', 'Hop-forward draft IPA', 'Toasty amber lager', 'Dry sparkling cider' and 'Dry sparkling rosé' each just restate the name's category. The wines print no grape origin or region. On the spirits page, the House Pours rows repeat the tequila subhead sensory text word for word.

STACK INCONSISTENCY: zero-proof items print only a sensory line. They have no ingredient line and no garnish · glass line, which breaks Rob's item stack on 4 items. Nojito's 'Mint, lime, soda' is an ingredient list set in the sensory treatment. Carajillo's last line is just 'rocks' (garnish null in the manifest), which reads as a missing fact.

LAYOUT (14): Brut Rosé $13 is printed without a glass or bottle label (manifest needs_input 5: 'glass or bottle unknown'). It is not ringed because it is approved_db, so the open question is invisible to the guest and to Rob. On the back table the price column sits about 1350 px from the names. The full-width row rules carry the eye, so the menu_item_association gate passes, but the 'class' column repeats every subhead and adds travel.

VENUE FIT (13): the bilingual heads are correct Spanish (Clásicos, De la Casa, Sin alcohol, Destilados, De barril, En lata, Por copa, Espumosos). The Batanga, Carajillo, Jamaica and horchata selection and the 25-pour agave depth read as a real cantina. The Milpa and Loess signatures tie the menu to Iowa (Iowa City, college-town tier). Two weak points: the page legend 'Agave hileras · Jalisco' heads a list that includes Oaxaca mezcal and Guanajuato tequila (it is art copy, not an item fact, so the gate passes), and Tecate is called 'Light Mexican lager', which a guest can misread as Tecate Light.
NOT INSPECTED: I did not open the phone preview (protocol call limit). The phone content rests on gates.json content_phone (50/50 pass).
fixes: Designer: keep each ingredient phrase and each 'garnish · glass' unit on one line (non-breaking spaces inside phrases, breaks only at the ' · ' separators) so no ingredient name or single word such as 'soda', 'lime' or 'syrup' is left alone on a line.

Content lead: print the Manhattan build as 'rye whiskey · sweet vermouth · aromatic bitters' per phg.menu_items (rv 9fb77eaa), and print Casa Noble NOM 1137 per public.brands 'Cn Casa Noble' / 'Marques de Casa Noble'.

Content lead: label Brut Rosé as glass or bottle, or ring it as pending (needs_input 5); resolve the Hornitos region against Tres Generaciones on NOM 1102; mark Vida, Montelobos and 400 Conejos as joven so all four mezcals share the unaged dot.

Content lead: replace the taxonomy beer and wine lines with sourced sensory copy, adding grape origin or region for the wines only if a row supports it; say 'Mexican lager' for Tecate; and stop repeating the tequila subhead text on the House Pours rows.
Designer: give the zero-proof items the same stack (sensory, ingredients, glass), take Cognac VSOP off the 'NOM class' oak axis or re-caption the axis, and fill or drop Carajillo's lone 'rocks' line.

lens: description quality and single guest-facing voice (criteria 10-14), K1 HILERAS, source = expanded-v1/manifest.json
top_problem: The menu uses two voices. The front speaks to the guest in sensory lines ("Smoke, bitter orange, velvet", "Green heat, ripe pineapple"). The back reads like database output. Beer, wine and cider print the raw phg.menu_items.menu_description class strings verbatim, and most of them only repeat the item name: Czech Pilsner 'Crisp pale lager', Dry-Hopped IPA 'Hop-forward draft IPA', Amber Lager 'Toasty amber lager', Dry Cider 'Dry sparkling cider', Brut Rosé 'Dry sparkling rosé', Malbec 'Dry red wine', Pinot Grigio 'Dry white wine'. 'Dry' appears 5 times in 9 rows. The spirits table then speaks in survey labels a guest cannot use ('class', 'NOM 1440', 'mo oak', '$'), and the 'class' column repeats the group head on every row ('TEQUILA · BLANCO' followed by 'blanco' 7 times). Criterion 12 automatic-fail wording applies to the beer and wine block.
verified: Margarita: rocks and lime wheel match rv f06abb74 (glassware 'Rocks', garnish 'Lime wheel'). Its sensory line 'Bright and citrus-forward' matches mi.menu_description. It is the only cocktail sensory line with a DB source.
Manhattan: coupe and cocktail cherry match rv 9fb77eaa. The DB description lists aromatic bitters. The menu hides the bitters on purpose (manifest note: public_components).
Brown Butter Old Fashioned: rocks and orange peel match rv 7095fd3d. The ingredients follow the DB description.
House Daiquiri: coupe and lime coin match rv 14d45e57. The ingredients match 'White rum, lime, and house demerara syrup'.
Beer, wine and cider sensory lines are the exact phg.menu_items.menu_description strings. They are sourced, but they are taxonomy, not description.

Blanco Tequila, Añejo Tequila and Cognac VSOP: the DB has only 'X pour.' The class lines ('Unaged · peppery…', '1–3 years oak…', '4+ years oak · stone fruit, toffee') come from the manifest's class-level draft. They trace to the manifest but are 'draft, not tasted'.
Every non-approved_db row carries the ring, the key is printed on both pages, and the NOM and region values match the manifest row for row.
problems: [12] The beer, wine and cider descriptions are class labels that restate the name (7 of 9 rows). The wines give no region or producer, so Malbec and Pinot Grigio print only a grape and a colour.

[12] The zero-proof lines break the stack and the voice. 'Mint, lime, soda' (Nojito) is an ingredient list presented as a sensory line. 'Mexican fruit soda; ask for flavors' (Jarritos) is server instruction in a different register and is the only line with a semicolon. 'Rice, cinnamon, creamy' mixes nouns and an adjective. Zero-proof items also have no ingredient line and no garnish · glass line, which Rob's binding stack requires. The manifest has no data for either, so this should be flagged missing_ingredients, not silently dropped.

[12] The cocktail sensory lines switch grammar: adjective triads ('Deep, spiced, silky', 'Nutty, round, warm', 'Crisp, clean, lightly rich') sit next to noun lists ('Espresso, vanilla, bittersweet', 'Toasted corn, cacao, oak'). 'Crisp, clean, lightly rich' contradicts itself and says nothing specific. 'Bright and citrus-forward' is trade jargon. All cocktail sensory lines except the Margarita's are sensory_status draft_not_tasted, yet they print unmarked on approved items (Manhattan, Brown Butter OF, House Daiquiri).

[12] Class sensory lines are printed twice. 'Unaged · peppery, bright cooked agave' appears under House Blanco Tequila and again in the TEQUILA · BLANCO head, and '1–3 years oak · caramel, dried fruit, baking spice' under House Añejo and again in the AÑEJO head. That breaks the proposal's own rule to print the class line once.

[11] Hornitos Reposado and Tres Generaciones Añejo share NOM 1102, yet one prints region '—' and the other 'Tequila Valley'. The same distillery gets two answers on one table (source: manifest spirits rows, where the region is null for Hornitos). A careful guest will read this as an error.
[11] Cognac VSOP is plotted on an oak axis whose legend says 'months in oak (NOM class)'. NOM-006 governs tequila, not cognac, so the legend misattributes the Cognac VSOP '4+ years' mark.

[11] Spicy Pineapple Margarita prints as 'jalapeño-infused tequila blanco · fresh pineapple' with no citrus or liqueur. The manifest source says 'confirm liqueur/citrus', and the item carries no missing-ingredient cue beyond the general proposal ring. A guest reads a two-ingredient 'margarita'.

[14] Single-word runts on ingredient lines: 'soda' (Paloma), 'lime' (House Daiquiri), 'pineapple' (Spicy Pineapple Margarita), 'fresh lime' (Margarita), 'mineral water' (Ranch Water). The measure is about 3 to 4 characters too short for the ingredient strings.

[14] Brut Rosé sits under 'ESPUMOSOS · SPARKLING' directly below 'POR COPA · BY THE GLASS', so it reads as a glass pour, but the manifest says 'glass or bottle unknown (needs_input 5)'. The pour is unlabelled and implied. 'Ranch Water 11.50' is the only price with decimals on a whole-dollar menu.

[13] The Spanish/English bilingual heads are correct and consistent (Clásicos, De la Casa, Destilados, Cerveza y sidra, De barril, En lata, Por copa, Espumosos, Sin alcohol). NOM numbers and 'mo oak' are aficionado data, though, and for a college-town Iowa City guest they are not translated into choice language. The back page reads as a spec sheet, not a cantina.
fixes: Replace the 7 name-repeating beer, wine and cider lines with guest-voice sensory lines in the same 3-beat register as the cocktails. Flag them draft_not_tasted, add region or producer for the wines, and send the needs_input request before printing.

Unify every sensory line under one grammar (three concrete tasting nouns or three adjectives, not both). Rewrite 'Crisp, clean, lightly rich', 'Bright and citrus-forward' and Jarritos' 'ask for flavors' to fit it, and mark draft_not_tasted lines on approved items in the proposal notes.

Designer note: remove the per-row 'class' column (it repeats the group head), print each class sensory line once, and give 'NOM' a one-line guest gloss in the legend (for example 'NOM = distillery number'). The legend should read 'months in oak (class minimum)' so the Cognac VSOP mark is not called NOM.

Resolve the NOM 1102 region conflict (Hornitos '—' against Tres Generaciones 'Tequila Valley') from one brand-graph row. Add a visible missing_ingredients flag to Spicy Pineapple Margarita and to the zero-proof items that have no ingredient or glass line.

Designer note: widen the ingredient measure or adjust tracking to kill the one-word runts. Label or separate Brut Rosé's pour until needs_input 5 is answered, and normalise 11.50 to the menu's whole-dollar style only if the source price allows it (otherwise print all prices with decimals).

lens: Venue fit for a Mexican restaurant and cocktail bar in Iowa City, Iowa (census context), plus ingredient accuracy, description quality and how descriptions sit with prices
top_problem: Every printed fact traces to expanded-v1/manifest.json, and the NOM, region, class and oak ranges I checked hold up (Corralejo 1368 Guanajuato, Herradura 1119 and Fortaleza 1493 Tequila Valley, El Tesoro 1139 Los Altos, reposado 2-12 mo, añejo 1-3 yr). But the menu does not yet read or sell like an Iowa City cantina. The census rows are phg_census_zcta 52240, 52245 and 52246: median household income $52,960 / $78,020 / $62,521, 21-34 share 29.9 / 29.1 / 36.9%, median age 28.3-31.8, Hispanic/Latino 5.4-11%. That is a young college-town crowd on a budget, yet the menu opens its house list with a $16 bourbon Brown Butter Old Fashioned and puts the Manhattan inside 'Clásicos' between Ranch Water and Batanga. The house pour tier is upside down on the back: Blanco Tequila $12 sits above Espolòn Blanco $11 and level with Patrón Silver $12; Hornitos Reposado $9 undercuts the house blanco; house Añejo is $16 against Tres Generaciones $20. The beer, cider and wine lines are taxonomy that restates the name ('Toasty amber lager', 'Hop-forward draft IPA', 'Dry sparkling cider', 'Dry red wine', 'Dry sparkling rosé'). No gate fails, because every row has a manifest source and every PROPOSED or rob_reference_image row carries the ring. Still, the untasted sensory lines on approved_db rows (Manhattan, Brown Butter Old Fashioned, House Daiquiri, all sensory_status draft_not_tasted) print with no ring, so a guest reads them as settled.
fixes: Venue notes for Rob and the designer, since item order and prices are not mine to change. Lead Clásicos with the agave drinks: Margarita, Paloma, Ranch Water, Batanga, Carajillo, then Manhattan. Lead De la Casa with Milpa Old Fashioned, Mezcal Negroni and Loess, so the Iowa-corn-meets-Jalisco drink is the first thing read instead of a bourbon Old Fashioned. Ask Rob to fix the house pour inversion (house Blanco $12 above Espolòn $11 and Hornitos Reposado $9) before print, because this price-sensitive college-town guest will notice it.

Criterion 12: rewrite the beer, cider and wine lines as guest language, taken only from source rows once the brewery, ABV, grape region or producer are supplied through needs_input. Until then flag them missing_ingredients rather than print name-echo taxonomy such as 'Dry white wine' under Pinot Grigio. Make Jarritos ('ask for flavors') and Nojito ('Mint, lime, soda') match the sensory voice of the other lines.

Criterion 14: keep each ingredient phrase whole with non-breaking spaces. The front now splits single ingredients across lines: 'grapefruit / soda' (Paloma), 'sparkling / mineral water' (Ranch Water), 'fresh / lime' (House Daiquiri), 'house / demerara syrup' (Brown Butter Old Fashioned), 'fresh / pineapple' (Spicy Pineapple Margarita), 'house roasted-corn / syrup' (Milpa), 'Iowa wildflower honey / syrup' (Loess). Clear the zero-proof widows ('lightly / sweet', 'ask / for flavors') as well.

Criterion 14 / 11: Brut Rosé $13 prints under 'Espumosos · Sparkling' with no glass or bottle label, and the manifest note says 'glass or bottle unknown (needs_input 5)'. Hold it for Rob's answer or show the needs-input flag. Also note that Ranch Water's '11.50' is the only price with decimals against whole-dollar prices everywhere else (a content-reviewer and Rob decision).

Criterion 11 / 13: Spicy Pineapple Margarita prints as complete with only 'jalapeño-infused tequila blanco · fresh pineapple', but the manifest source says 'confirm liqueur/citrus'. The Manhattan omits bitters (rv 9fb77eaa public_components hides them). A guest ordering a margarita with no lime printed will ask, so mark both specs as incomplete, or confirm them with Rob before print. Also extend the proposal key, or add a 'draft tasting notes' mark, to the approved_db rows whose sensory lines are draft_not_tasted.

lens: How descriptions and prices sit together in the print PNGs (preview-front.png and preview-back.png at 2550x3300), plus the price-to-item gate, checked against expanded-v1/manifest.json
top_problem: The ingredient lines break inside an ingredient name, so one ingredient gets split across two lines and a single word is left alone on the second. Examples: Paloma 'grapefruit / soda' (manifest: 'grapefruit soda'), Ranch Water 'sparkling / mineral water', House Daiquiri 'fresh / lime', Spicy Pineapple Margarita 'fresh / pineapple', Milpa Old Fashioned 'house roasted-corn / syrup', Loess 'Iowa wildflower honey / syrup', Brown Butter Old Fashioned 'house / demerara syrup'. That is 7 of the 12 cocktails. The zero-proof sensory lines also leave single words behind ('lightly / sweet', 'ask / for flavors'). Beside Rob's reference boards this is the most visible layout flaw, and it breaks Rob's binding ingredient-line rule by printing an ingredient that is not in the manifest as written. Other checks: every printed name, price, sensory line, ingredient, garnish, glass, class, NOM number and region matches its manifest row exactly. Every proposed row carries the ring, and no approved row does. Front prices sit inline, about 0.5 em after the name. Back prices are far right, but each row has its own full-width row rule, so both gates pass. Also flagged: (a) The price 11.50 (Ranch Water) is the only price with decimals among whole numbers. (b) Brut Rosé 13 sits under 'ESPUMOSOS · SPARKLING' with no glass or bottle label; the manifest itself says glass or bottle is unknown (needs_input 5). (c) The 25 spirit prices have no pour label. The manifest's pour_size says 1.5 oz is 'proposed … not established', so the designer rightly left it off; Rob needs to decide the pour size. (d) The back legend says 'months in oak (NOM class)', but it also covers the Cognac VSOP arrow. Cognac is not graded by a NOM class; the manifest's sensory_status wrongly cites NOM-006 for it. (e) The beer and wine lines read like database categories ('Dry red wine', 'Dry white wine', 'Hop-forward draft IPA', 'Crisp pale lager'). The IPA line repeats the item name. None shows ABV, grape or region, because the manifest has none. (f) On the front, the rule after each price runs straight into the next column's proposal ring, so the ring for Paloma, Batanga, Carajillo and Ranch Water reads as the end of the rule from the item on its left. That makes it unclear which item is proposed; the prices themselves stay attached.
